Map.tabMapExplainer: Every box is a point from the submissions — sorted into zones (resolvable by evidence vs. politically decided) and by the premise of the core argument it negotiates. Click a point for its camp profile, statement, and original quotes.
Map.tabAnalysisExplainer: Participants who vote alike form camps. Bridges hold across all camps; conflict lines show where exactly they divide — sorted by the depth of the divide.

Report.methodNote: Method: statements were voted agree/disagree/pass; camps are opinion clusters (PCA + k-means, k chosen by silhouette); bridges and conflict lines follow Polis-style significance tests; the diagnosis is computed deterministically from configured thresholds. Points were extracted from submissions by a language model and released editorially; every step is audit-logged.

Home.eyebrow: An open-source tool for real participation
Home.title: The map of the dispute
Home.lead: policy turns thousands of free-text submissions into a readable picture: who claims what, where the camps agree, where exactly they divide — and which disputes evidence could settle versus what must be decided politically.
Home.zoneExpertsText: Factual questions that evidence can settle — for the price of an expert report.
Home.zoneCouncilText: Value questions no study can decide — politics must decide and own these.
